data.answer: Geek Chic has been making lifestyle furniture for geeks since 2008, starting with gaming tables and expanding into other geek needs like comic storage, collectibles display, and office retrofitting. Each heirloom quality piece is handcrafted by a small team of dedicated woodworkers in a shop just north of Seattle, WA. The company is based in Everett, Washington, and has 41 employees. Geek Chic is a furniture and home furnishings manufacturer based in Everett, Washington. Since 2008, the company has produced lifestyle furniture for geeks, beginning with gaming tables and expanding into storage for comics, displays for collectibles, and retrofitted office spaces. Its products are handcrafted by a small team of woodworkers in a shop north of Seattle, reflecting a focus on heirloom quality. The target market includes individuals seeking specialized, characterful furniture that supports both display and practical use, addressing needs related to personal collections, gaming, and work environments. The business sits within the furniture and home furnishings manufacturing sector and emphasizes durable, craft-focused pieces as part of its offering.

results.content:
Title: Geek Chic from Shark Tank - Seriosity
# Geek Chic from Shark Tank. A custom-made heirloom-quality gaming-themed piece of furniture by Robert Gifford was featured in Shark Tank. In Everett, WA, he created Geek Chic furniture for the discerning gamer/geek who values both usefulness and aesthetics. Geek Chic’s gaming tables can be entirely modified to suit the gaming preferences and aesthetics of the consumer. In terms of gaming tables, Geek Chic can create cozy card games, epic RPG battles, and everything in between. Gifford has been playing role-playing games for 40 years and has decided to turn his hobby into a business to help others who share his love of games. Robert Gifford introduced the Tank audience to the world of Geek Chic. As a demonstration, Gifford showed off one of his dining tables that can be converted into a gaming area. On the other hand, Robert Herjavec did not believe in the business strategy of the furniture company. Daymond John had fallen head over heels in love with the furniture and how Gifford handled his business. With a Shark agreement in hand, Gifford accepted Herjavec’s offer. As a real “geek,” Gifford went through the offer in great depth after the Shark Tank and ultimately decided to go with another investor. However, the Geek Chic company had to start making money. Geek Chic tables were a gamer’s haven, to say the least. Most geeks and gamers who saw the furniture for the first time were awestruck. Gaming tables typically cost a boatload of money. Therefore, most people utilize their dining tables to accommodate their gaming ventures. Geek Chic’s booth could be placed in a gaming room or even a few feet from your work desk. You could pay D&D, witches of warcraft, and many other games on this handy table. Geek Chic was introduced explicitly for gamers and geeks curious about how the world works. Those who want to create a game cave in their home and store their vintage games in a secure location would have found the furniture of Geek Chic convenient. The best alternative for Geek Chic is Board Games Table (BGT). It is still in business and offers the furniture at a reasonable price. Geek Chic was a gamer’s heaven.
